brief: UBS's Perl did not expect Thursday's (05-Nov) equity sell-off but argues it is not the end of the bull market: SPX stays on track for his 8,485 target next year, so he recommends against selling into weakness given risk/reward skewed to the topside into year-end and beyond. Cross-asset, damage was contained outside Japan (which he says to avoid) and South Korea; SX5E, Hang Seng (developing a Wave 3 on daily, weekly and monthly charts) and Australia held up, and Mexico and India (which he has been bullish on for the past month) are up, which he reads as de-risking rather than de-leveraging, consistent with his view that the sell-off was corrective within the broader advance rather than its end. SOX, the epicenter of the de-risking, printed a TD Combo 11 Count with both daily and weekly TD Propulsion downside targets hit at the low, a confluence that typically precedes a tradable rebound; a Combo 13 Buy could come as soon as Monday's (09-Nov) close. NDX lags by a day (Combo 10), and the SPW/NDX ratio's Combo 11 could flip to a Sell (13) the same day.
